messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — noticed a handful of eval traces uploaded last night where the per-sample `outputs` field is cut off mid-JSON. Looks like metadata.user_id is missing too. :thinking_face:
Samir Patel: hmm. Do you have an example object key?
Maria Chen: TraceBot posted the upload in #eval-runner logs:
TraceBot: Trace uploaded s3://redwood-eval-traces/2026/03/18/trace-1815129999-abc123.json.gz (size=11.2KB) :robot_face:
Maria Chen: When I downloaded and gunzipped it the sample array ends with `..., "outputs": {"tokens": ["hello", "worl` and then EOF.
Devin Brooks: That looks like truncation during chunked upload or the gzip writer closing early. We had a similar one for multipart gzip >8KB before but fixed the boundary bug.
Samir Patel: Is this only for quantized-runner jobs or all evals?
Maria Chen: Only quantization experiments so far — those traces tend to be slightly bigger (extra per-token logs + kv snapshots).
Olivia Kim: Could also be the runner's `trace_max_bytes` config. Current default is 10_000 (bytes) in `eval-runner.conf` and we do a hard truncate at write. If truncation happens inside a JSON token that yields invalid JSON after gzip decompress.
Devin Brooks: Right. We should never produce invalid JSON artifacts. Two quick fixes: 1) atomically write to a temp file then gzip and upload; 2) ensure truncation happens at sample boundary and add a `truncated: true` flag.
Samir Patel: Also we need to avoid accidentally dropping PII. I saw metadata.user_id gone in a couple of samples. That might be a sanitizer that strips `user_id` but only runs in-memory before chunking — if chunk happens mid-record the final chunk may not include the sanitized header.
Maria Chen: Repro steps I ran:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-eval-traces/2026/03/18/trace-1815129999-abc123.json.gz - | gunzip -c > trace.json
jq -r '.samples[] | select(.metadata.user_id == null) | .id' trace.json | head
```
I got 5 sample ids.
Olivia Kim: Proposal: Change schema so PII is stored under `metadata.pii_hash` (one-way) and keep `metadata.sanitized` for downstream checks. That reduces risk if something gets trimmed.
Samir Patel: Agree. Also add a CI sanity test that fetches newly uploaded trace artifacts in PR builds and validates: 1) JSON parseable 2) presence of required keys `id`, `inputs`, `outputs` 3) `metadata` contains either `pii_hash` or `sanitized:true`. Put test under `eng-ml/eval-harness/tests/test_trace_integrity.py`.
Devin Brooks: I'll sketch the fix: ensure stream writer buffers full sample objects before gzip/streaming and atomically uploads final file. If upload fails due to size cap we rotate and mark `truncated: true` at the sample boundary.
Maria Chen: Can someone pick up the immediate mitigation? Add a short lambda that scans last 24h uploads and alerts on non-parseable gz files.
Samir Patel: I'll open a PR for the CI check + small detector lambda. ETA EOD tomorrow. Assigning to me. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: Thanks — created a minimal dashboard query in Logs to surface `Trace: parse_error` events. Adding that to the incident runbook.
TraceBot: New alert rule created: `eval.trace_parse_error > 0` (notify #eng-oncall) :robot_face:
Olivia Kim: Cool. After Samir's PR we should also draft a migration to populate `pii_hash` for recent runs and a backfill to mark any truncated traces.
Samir Patel: Will include a migration plan in the PR description.
Maria Chen: Great — let's sync tomorrow in 10m channel if anyone wants to pair on reproducing. :eyes:
